value.rationale: The 2026 Lp skew Schäffer formula leaves a concrete one-parameter matrix-norm optimization. At a fixed nonendpoint skew, the row-Hölder bound is an exact explicit benchmark that agrees with the true matrix norm to all algebraic orders in \(1/p\). Determining the first nonzero exponentially small excess with a sharp τ-dependent coefficient and proving which projective directions attain it reveals a genuine singular high-p feature of a natural Banach-space geometric constant. It is neither merely the \(p=\infty\) norm nor a routine endpoint substitution; the proof requires global maximizing-direction classification and a second-scale Taylor estimate.
